attachments.origin_landmark: greater and lesser horns of the hyoid and the stylohyoid ligament

actions: constricts the middle pharynx, propelling the bolus during swallowing

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Overlapped from below by the inferior constrictor and overlapping the superior -- the telescoped arrangement that produces the sequential stripping wave of pharyngeal swallowing.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- the only clinical BoNT literature found treats the middle and inferior pharyngeal constrictors as a single spastic mass ("pharyngoesophageal segment") in laryngectomized patients who cannot produce tracheoesophageal voice, and does not separately localize middle-constrictor injection. Technique: a single percutaneous injection, unilaterally, into the constrictor mass, performed under EMG guidance with the needle placement confirmed by recorded muscle activity during attempted phonation; a parapharyngeal (Carbocaine) nerve block was used beforehand to confirm that relaxing the constrictors would restore voice.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG activity recorded during attempted tracheoesophageal phonation confirms the needle is within the spastic constrictor mass; effect confirmed post-injection by low-amplitude or absent EMG activity in the treated muscle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: This is a narrow, non-standard indication (post-laryngectomy pharyngoesophageal spasm/voice failure), not a typical spasticity or dystonia target, and the source literature does not distinguish middle from inferior constrictor fibers when injecting -- reported here with that caveat rather than a muscle-specific technique. Doses reported: 100 U (10 of 12 patients) or 50 U (2 of 12) unilaterally at one location; effect apparent at 24-48 h and long-lasting in most. No dedicated ultrasound-guided technique for this muscle was found.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Bartolomei L, Zambito Marsala S, Pighi GP, Cristofori V, Pagano G, Pontarin M, Gioulis M, Marchini C, 'Botulinum toxin type A: an effective treatment to restore phonation in laryngectomized patients unable to voice', Neurol Sci 32(3):443-447 (2011), doi:10.1007/s10072-011-0560-1 -- retrieved via PubMed.
